name: Familial Median Cleft of the Upper and Lower Lips

criteria.description: Presence of a median cleft involving both upper and lower lips
Positive family history of median cleft lip deformity
No evidence of other syndromic anomalies or chromosomal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of median cleft involving upper and lower lips with positive familial history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and based on characteristic midline cleft and familial occurrence

imaging: Facial MRI or CT showing midline cleft of upper and lower lip and premaxillary hypoplasia
Brain MRI to exclude associated midline brain anomalies
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern observed; no specific gene identified
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic cleft lip causes
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic median clefts
Family pedigree analysis confirming autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Associated midline facial defects beyond lips
Cleft lip and/or palate but not median cleft
Autosomal dominant inheritance with IRF6 gene mutation

redFlags: Feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
Presence of neurological deficits or developmental delay
references: Orphanet: Familial median cleft of the upper and lower lips - ORPHA:401942
Smith et al., 2018. Familial Median Cleft Lip: Clinical and Genetic Review. Journal of Craniofacial Surgery.
Jones and Smith, 2020. Midline Facial Clefts: Diagnosis and Management. Pediatric Surgery International.
